article.title: Incremental indexing
article.heading: How we made our search index incremental
article.lead: For three years, every change to our product catalog triggered a full rebuild of the search index. As the catalog grew to 40 million listings, that nightly job stretched past six hours. Here is how we moved to incremental indexing, and what it cost us.
article.why: A full rebuild was simple and always consistent, but it meant that a price change made at 9 a.m. would not be searchable until the next morning. Sellers noticed. Support tickets about “missing” listings tripled over two quarters.
article.figcaption: Median indexing time per day, before and after the migration.
article.approach: We split the index into 512 shards keyed by listing ID and stream changes from the catalog’s change log into a queue. Each shard worker applies updates in small batches and publishes a new segment every 30 seconds.
points: Writes are idempotent, so replays after a crash are safe.
A nightly `compact` job merges small segments to keep queries fast.
A shadow index ran for six weeks before we switched traffic.
article.cost: Storage grew by about 18% because of unmerged segments, and on-call load went up for the first month while we tuned batch sizes.
